market_summary:
Wall Street suffered its worst session in months on 5 Nov as the Nasdaq Composite erased ~$2.5T in value on fears that a Democratic-controlled Congress could tighten regulation on AI data-center buildout; QQQ fell 5.6% and entered correction territory, SPY fell 2.8%, with NVDA (-12.1%), TSLA (-13.8%), GOOGL and META all hit hard, while AAPL (+3.7%) and MSFT held up comparatively well. In Singapore, the big three banks reported Q3 results this week with divergent outcomes: OCBC beat estimates and raised 2026 loan-growth guidance, DBS beat on profit and lifted its dividend sharply (though flagged flat-to-down 2026 profit), while UOB missed estimates and cut its NIM outlook, with elevated trading volume confirming distribution. SGX bank stocks have already de-rated 8-13% over the past month on rate and margin worries, so post-earnings reactions are diverging by name. Overall risk sentiment is fragile and headline-driven, favoring tactical, name-specific positioning over broad index bets until the AI-regulation narrative and Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings clarify the picture.</market_summary>
